original_question: Describe an open subset of an irreducible component of Hilb_d(A^3) that is different from the smoothable component, allowing d to be large.
target_in_paper: §2.1, Problem VII: "Describe (an open subset of) a component of Hilb_d(A^n) other than the smoothable one. Here n can be a large integer, even n=3." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core mathematical task of Problem VII: it asks for a description of an open subset/general point of a component of a Hilbert scheme of points that is not the smoothable component, and it focuses on the especially interesting case A^3, which the paper explicitly says would already be significant. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
missing_details: The nearest official formulation is for Hilb_d(A^n), not only Hilb_d(A^3); moreover, the paper says that n may be large, even n=3, so the parameter allowed to be large in the statement is the ambient dimension n, not the degree d. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
The base field should be specified: throughout §1.3 the paper works over an algebraically closed field k. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
Hilb_d(X) should be defined explicitly as the Hilbert scheme of finite subschemes of X of degree d. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

The smoothable component should be defined explicitly as the closure of the open locus of smooth degree-d subschemes of A_k^n; in affine space this is the locus of d distinct k-points. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

The official problem is existential and local on one component: it asks for describing a nonempty open subset of some non-smoothable irreducible component, not for classifying all components and not for doing this for every, arbitrarily large, or sufficiently large d. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

If one insists on the specialization to A^3, the nearby characteristic-zero summary matters: the paper records that Hilb_d(A^3) is irreducible precisely for d≤11 and reducible for d≥12, so a component different from the smoothable one can only occur once d is in the reducible range. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))

No extra hypotheses such as punctuality, Gorenstein, local, graded, or complete-intersection conditions belong to Problem VII; it concerns the ordinary Hilbert scheme of points on affine space. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
refined_question: Over an algebraically closed field k, find positive integers d and n and describe a nonempty open subset of an irreducible component of Hilb_d(A_k^n), the Hilbert scheme of degree-d finite subschemes of affine n-space, that is distinct from the smoothable component (the closure of the open locus of smooth degree-d subschemes, equivalently of d distinct k-points). As emphasized in the paper, the ambient dimension n may be large, and it would already be significant to do this even for n=3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
justification: This is Problem VII rather than Problem VIII. The wording "describe (an open subset of) a component ... other than the smoothable one" matches Problem VII essentially verbatim, whereas Problem VIII asks for the broader task of classifying all components for small n such as n=3. To make the problem stand alone, one has to import from §1.3 the base-field convention and the meaning of Hilb_d(X), and from the opening of §2.1 the definition of the smoothable component. Because your draft hard-codes A^3, the nearby characteristic-zero context is also relevant: the paper notes that Hilb_d(A^3) is irreducible for d≤11 and reducible for d≥12. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2307.08777))
